answer: Temporal diversity at the knoll: each ID must submit within a randomized 90-second window derived from its stake hash, so one operator cannot batch-prove many IDs in the same slot. The nebula of open timestamps exposes correlated bursts, and colluding clusters face the walnut: a 40% detection fine per flagged batch. Farming 100 IDs needs ~100 distinct live windows, costing ~$3,400 in rented uptime plus forfeited stakes. This works because randomized timing converts cheap parallelism into expensive, detectable serialization.
